title: What If You Flew Through the Van Allen Radiation Belts?

scenes.text: What if you flew straight through the Van Allen radiation belts? Apollo crews did, twice.
The inner belt starts about 700 kilometers up and reaches roughly 10,000. The outer belt lies farther out.
Apollo's route crossed both in only a few hours. Crews were beyond the belts within about ten hours of launch.
Across nine lunar missions, crews averaged just 0.46 rad, less than a chest CT scan.
The lowest was 0.16 on Apollo 8. The highest was 1.14 on Apollo 14, with much of it from the belt crossings.
The bigger danger was a solar storm. One in August 1972 fell between Apollo 16 and 17, and could have forced an emergency return.
